A loop is not a song. **Arranging** is laying parts out along the timeline so the song has sections (intro, verse, chorus, bridge,
outro) and changes as it goes: instruments come in and drop out, the drums get busier for the chorus, everything stops for a beat.
In a DAW you arrange by moving **clips** (Logic and BandLab call them **regions**) on the tracks.

## Session players

Instead of writing every part, let the band write a start. Under the tracks, type chords (bars split by `|`), pick a **Style** and press
**Write the parts**: the Backing Track band's drummer, bassist and chord player each write their part into a clip at the playhead.
Logic's **Drummer** and **Session Players**, BandLab's **SongStarter** and Ableton's MIDI generators do the same job. The parts are now
ordinary MIDI clips: open them in the editor and change any note.

**Feel.** The band's patterns sit *exactly* on the grid. When the Backing Track plays them it adds the small human touches a real band has: the bass a few
milliseconds ahead of the beat and the chords a few behind it, a little random looseness, chords rolled from the bottom note up (a guitar strum a bit slower), and velocities that wander a little.
The **Feel** menu writes those touches into the clips: **Tight** (on the grid, the default), **Band feel** (as the Backing Track plays) or **Looser** (twice as much). **Humanize clip** does the same to a clip you
already have, once; **Quantize** takes it out again. The tempo stays perfectly steady in all of them, as it does in the live band: a human band would also push and pull the tempo, and neither this DAW nor the band does that.

## Build a song

1. Press **Write the parts** with *C | Am | F | G*, Rock, 2 times. That's 8 bars: call it the **verse**.
2. Move the playhead to bar 9 (click the ruler), type *F | G | C | Am* and write 2 times again: the **chorus**.
3. Select a clip and **Duplicate** (Ctrl/Cmd+D) to repeat a section. Set **Song** length longer first if you run out of room.
4. **Drop a part out**: delete the Chords clip in the first verse, or drag the drum clip later so the drums enter at bar 5.
   An arrangement is as much about who *isn't* playing.
5. **Split** a clip at the playhead (put the playhead inside the clip, press Split) and delete the second half for a stop.
6. Drag a clip by its right edge to change its length; drag the clip to move it (hold **Alt** to move by beats, not bars), or onto another track.
7. Try a different **Style** for the chorus only: the band rewrites the clips under it, the verse stays.

## Place clips from the keyboard

Click the DAW once so it has focus, then you can lay a song out without the mouse. These are this small DAW's own keys; they are not
claimed to match any other program.

| Keys | What happens |
|---|---|
| **←** **→** (or **h** **l**) | Playhead back / forward a bar (**Alt**: a beat) |
| **↑** **↓** (or **k** **j**) | Select the track above / below, and the clip under the playhead |
| **[** **]** | Select the previous / next clip on the track (the playhead jumps to it) |
| **N** | New empty clip on the track at the playhead |
| **P** | Put the Session clip you last selected (see [DAW 4b](daw-session.qmd)) on its track at the playhead; the playhead moves to its end, so **P P P** lays it three times |
| **Shift+←** **Shift+→** (or **H** **L**) | Move the selected clip a bar (**Alt**: a beat) |
| **Shift+↑** **Shift+↓** (or **K** **J**) | Move it to the track above / below (same kind of track) |
| **-** **=** | Make it a bar shorter / longer (**Alt**: a beat) |
| A **number** first (**3l**, **2j**, **3p**) | Repeat the next key that many times: three bars on, two tracks down, the Session clip laid three times |
| **O** | Loop on / off (it was **L**; **l** is now →) |
| **Ctrl/Cmd+D**, **Delete**, **Ctrl/Cmd+Z** | Duplicate, delete, undo |

Try it: ↓ to the Bass track, **N**, **→** four times, **N**, then **Shift+→** to slide it a bar.

## Common shapes

- **Build**: start with one or two instruments, add one every 4 or 8 bars.
- **Contrast**: verse sparse and low, chorus full and wide; a bridge in other chords.
- **Fewer is louder**: dropping the drums for two bars makes their return hit harder.
- Sections are usually **4, 8 or 16 bars**. The DAW's grid makes it easy to keep them that way.

Arranging for a band in more depth: [Arranging 1: Who Plays What](arrange-band.qmd). Naming sections: [Section labels](section-labels.qmd).

## In other DAWs

<div class="daw-map">

| | BandLab | Ableton Live | Logic Pro |
|---|---|---|---|
| A clip is called | Region | Clip | Region |
| Generated parts | **SongStarter**; loops | MIDI Generators (Live 12); loops from the browser | **Session Players**: Drummer, Bass Player, Keyboard Player |
| Duplicate | **Alt/Option-drag** | **Cmd/Ctrl+D** | Edit → Repeat |
| Split at the playhead | **S** (slice) | **Cmd/Ctrl+E** | Edit → Split → Regions at Playhead |
| Move without the grid | Turn snap off | **Cmd/Ctrl+4** turns the grid off | The Snap menu |
| Sections | Use region names / colours | Locators (Create → Add Locator) | **Arrangement track** (markers you can drag, copy and move whole sections) |

</div>
